title: Learning to tend bar from Kingfish; 'The Singing Bartender'
summary: Jesse Fisher (Kingfish) taught him bartending; clubs ran all night with gambling, and Turner sang between pouring drinks.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: So bartending was just as popular a profession during Prohibition as it was when drinking was legal?

Oh, yeah. Yes, indeed. I got a friend right now in Kansas City who's still tendin' bar. His name's Jesse Fisher. We call him Kingfish. I saw him about four...five years ago when I was there. He was tendin' bar aroun'...he's the one who learned me how to tend bar. 'Course, wasn't much to it. You hadda know the different whiskeys--the red and the white--sell soda pop, draw beer. And they had a big time [ ] the name bartender. He mixed all the different drinks, so when he would be mixing drinks, I would watch him. So he found out what I was doin', so when he get ready to mix a drink, he turn his back on me so I couldn't learn but he couldn't keep his back turned all the time.

When he get crowded, he have to make 'em up in a hurry, so he'd mix a drink, and I watch him, what he put in it and everything, you know. I learned how to mix up drinks. Wasn't too bad then 'cause they didn't have too many bigtime drinks anyway. 'Course, then, in them days, it was a regular routine, goin' to work at nine o'clock, gettin' off at five o'clock in the mornin'. Joint be open all night long. Between times, the band would take a hour...a half an hour break. Then you had the gamblin' goin' on in the back o' the place. All the tips they'd made, they go back there and try to gamble. It was just like up in Las Vegas there. Silver dollars stacked up. Look like you got a million dollars there. Ain't nothin' but about two...three hundred dollars' worth of silver dollars. The man set aback behind there...had a stick man who rake up the dice... regular routine. That's the way they did it.

I was brought up in learnin' all that stuff 'cause I saw it when I was young, you know, so it wasn't nothin' new to me. And I took my time and learnt how to bartend so when the...when the entertainers wasn't workin', I'd go up and get behind the bar. I learned how to tend bar, and I git up, go on with my apron and everything on, I get up there and sing for the people. They's call me "The Singing Bartender." That's what they knowed me by...kept me busy. So that was a lot of fun because I always wanted to sing anyway, and I took my own good time. I was ...

In between times, when I wasn't runnin' whiskey...well, I didn't want to go back too often 'cause I'd take two good pitchers, and while they be serving them, I go take two more. Couldn't bring too much 'cause it would be a waste. Y'hear the police comin', you have to throw it out. So I always keep a couple extra pitchers sittin' on the side where I stood at.

I was...I was a bartender but I was just a'pourin' out straight drinks...stuff like that. I wasn't slick as the bigshot was, makin' all that mixed drinks and stuff. He was good at it, y'know. I was just learnin'. In the meantime, I'm runnin' back, gettin' the whiskey an' everything, an' I'm takin' care of business.
